source: In the S bus, in the rush hour. A chap of about 26, felt hat with a cord instead of a ribbon, neck too long, as if someone’s been having a tug-of-war with it. People getting off. The chap in question gets annoyed with one of the men standing next to him. He accuses him of jostling him every time anyone goes past. A snivelling tone which is meant to be aggressive. When he sees a vacant seat he throws himself on to it. Two hours later, I meet him in the Cour de Rome, in front of the gare Saint-Lazare. He’s with a friend who’s saying: "You ought to get an extra button put on your overcoat." He shows him where (at the lapels) and why.

gens.text: In the aisle, a cart clashes with the conveyor belt. The cashier scans items quickly, her movements precise and practiced, each beep of the barcode reader marking the rhythm of the day. Behind her, the bagging area overflows with groceries, the plastic bags straining under the weight. A shopper taps impatiently, her eyes darting to the clock on the wall, while another customer, edging closer, mutters under his breath. The friction between them grows, a tension palpable in the air. Across the counter, the cashier announces the total, her voice steady and clear. She prompts for the loyalty card, the routine as familiar as breathing. The card reader blinks, and the transaction is complete. The receipt printer hums, spitting out the final tally. With a nod, the shopper gathers her bags and moves aside, making way for the next in line.

In the aisle, a cart rested near the conveyor. At the checkout, amidst the hum and beeps, the cashier scanned items with precision, while the shopper bagged groceries, the card reader ready. The line moved, the total announced, the receipt printed. Behind, another shopper edged closer, the divider bar a fragile boundary. Tensions rose, space scarce, the queue a tight fit. Loyalty cards were prompted, the routine of retail unbroken. Just then, a bag split, spilling contents. The cashier paused, the shopper sighed, the moment tense. Amid the chaos, the next in line waited, patience fraying. They glanced, a silent plea, the cart a barrier. The cashier resumed, the scanner beeped, the friction eased.
